about.title: Duarte Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Duarte residents rely on nearby Los Angeles County hospitals and clinics for everything from routine checkups to emergency care, and most visits go fine. But when a provider misses a clear warning sign, gives the wrong medication, or botches a surgical step, the damage can follow a patient for years. California's MICRA law shapes these cases in specific ways: claims generally must be filed within one year of discovering the harm (and no later than three years from the injury itself), a 90-day pre-suit notice is required before a lawsuit moves forward, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in to confirm the standard of care was breached. A poor result on its own isn't proof of malpractice — the law requires showing the provider fell below accepted medical standards. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly; we simply connect Duarte patients and families with an independent attorney who can review the facts and explain your options, free of charge.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Duarte?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred. A 90-day written notice to the provider is also required before a lawsuit can be filed. These deadlines are strict, so it helps to talk to an attorney as soon as you suspect something went wrong.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves risk, and a poor result by itself doesn't prove negligence. To have a valid claim, you generally need to show the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the case.
